title: Bezier patch decomposition changes valid splines
proof: For degree 2, knots [-1,-1,0,1,2,2] and poles (0,0), (1,1), (2,0), the decomposed midpoint has y=0.5; the spline has y=0.75. With knots [0,0,0,1,1,1,2,2,2] and x poles 0..5, the second span evaluates to x=3 instead of 4.
impact: Surface inversion and bounds consume patches that no longer represent the source surface. Endpoint clamping is missing; interval_index*degree also selects the wrong controls after full-multiplicity internal knots. The probe establishes patch corruption, not a complete codec conversion failure.
fix: Extract spans by their actual knot/control indices, including active endpoint insertion. Share the corrected algorithm with IGES; its copy has the same defects.

title: Surface Newton solver stops on a regular small plane
proof: A 1e-5 by 1e-5 bilinear plane, target (0.3e-5,0.4e-5,0), and seed (0,0) return (0,0), although one Newton step gives (0.3,0.4). The determinant is 1e-20 and is rejected against absolute machine epsilon.
impact: SolidWorks projection callers forward-check the candidate and can discard valid geometry. The API documents a candidate, so this is failed convergence, not a falsely claimed nearest-point certificate. Its separate absolute squared-distance stopping gate also prevents scale-independent accuracy.
fix: Scale the least-squares columns and use a relative rank test. Use a residual/parameter convergence contract that does not impose an undocumented absolute model-space floor.

title: Rational search speed bounds depend on common weight scale
proof: The same unit line has speed bound Some(1) with weights [1,1], but None with [1e-200,1e-200]. minimum_weight.powi(2) underflows, producing 0/0. The pcurve containment path repeats this formula.
impact: A geometrically unchanged curve loses parameter-witness and containment support before search starts. This is outside the point/tangent evaluators fixed in the previous audit.
fix: Normalize common weight scale or evaluate the bound through scale-safe ratios/products; retain a conservative upper bound.

title: Periodic parameter facade still returns Some(NaN)
proof: A periodic curve with domain [-1e308,-9e307] and finite parameter 1e308 returns Some(NaN): parameter-lower overflows before rem_euclid.
impact: Tangent, second-derivative, and model differential paths call this facade. The earlier periodic_parameter fix did not reach this separate implementation.
fix: Use the existing scale-safe periodic mapping implementation, and require a finite in-domain result.

title: Curve witness accepts a point outside zero tolerance
proof: For a unit X-axis line and point (0,1e-200,0), tolerance 0 returns the endpoint witness 0. The current squared-distance closure underflows to zero; the actual distance is 1e-200.
impact: The documented forward-residual guarantee is false for very small separations. This is an extreme-scale boundary case, not evidence of a problem at ordinary positive CAD tolerances.
fix: Use the shared scale-safe point distance in the boundary and interval residual checks.

title: Sweep-law quotient differentiation overflows avoidable intermediates
proof: At X=1, X/1e200 has derivative 0 instead of 1e-200. X/1e-200 returns None although its value and derivative, 1e200, are finite. The quotient rule squares the denominator.
impact: Valid law-driven sweep derivatives become zero or unavailable. The affected function feeds sweep surface differential evaluation.
fix: Evaluate the quotient derivative using scale-safe ratios/products instead of an unscaled squared denominator.

title: Hyperbolic sweep laws lose finite values and derivatives
proof: TANH at value 20 and incoming derivative 1e20 returns derivative 0; the stable result is about 1699.341702. ARCSINH at value/derivative 1e200 returns derivative 0 instead of approximately 1. ARCOTH(1e20) returns value 0 instead of approximately 1e-20.
impact: Cancellation in 1-tanh(x)^2 and (x+1)/(x-1), plus overflowing x*x, damages law values and chain-rule derivatives. These are one family in the same dispatch function.
fix: Use stable hyperbolic identities, hypot-based denominators, and log1p/atanh formulations with their domain checks.

title: Helix circular-frame admission still uses an unsafe norm
proof: The current admission expressions accept orthogonal equal-radius vectors at radius 1, but reject them at finite radii 1e200 and 1e-200. Squared lengths overflow or underflow before the radius comparison.
impact: Finite circular helix constructions are refused even though the shared Vector3 norm now handles these scales. This is an extreme-scale admission defect.
fix: Use the shared norm for both radii and preserve the existing acceptance tolerance.

title: Wrong Bezier spans can certify unequal surface boundaries
proof: The same unclamped and discontinuous examples as IR2-01 produce wrong spans. Two degree-2 curves with full internal multiplicity that differ only at their final control point are reported equal at resolution 0; their separation at t=1.5 is 1.
impact: The Type 128 closed-surface flag check can accept inconsistent boundaries. The same decomposition also feeds aligned rails for ruled surfaces. This duplicate algorithm has already drifted from the corrected Rhino implementation.
fix: Use one corrected shared Bezier extraction algorithm; test both active endpoint clipping and degree+1 interior multiplicity.

title: Boundary equality underflows after multiplying homogeneous weights
proof: Two parallel unit lines separated by 2, both weighted [1e-200,1e-200], compare equal at resolution 1e-6. Both cross-products and the threshold underflow to zero.
impact: Closure admission can accept genuinely open boundaries with ordinary coordinates. Normalizing the common weight scale must not change the answer.
fix: Scale the homogeneous operands before cross-products and compare a scale-safe residual against the resolution.

title: Second line–arc intersection implementation retains the false-tangent bug
proof: A line from (-1e-4,2e-4) to (1e-4,2e-4) and circle of radius 1e-4 at the origin are disjoint. The boolean routine returns true while the corrected point-producing routine returns no intersections.
impact: Profile independence and containment decisions can reject valid disjoint loops. The .max(1.0) discriminant error floor remains in the boolean copy.
fix: Route the boolean decision through the corrected intersection owner and remove the duplicate quadratic solver.

title: Profile NURBS speed bounds fail under common weight scaling
proof: The same unit pcurve has bound Some(1) with weights [1,1] and None with [1e-200,1e-200]. The unscaled squared minimum weight produces 0/0.
impact: Certified profile-tube and separation paths refuse an unchanged valid profile. This is another local copy of the rational-bound problem.
fix: Share a scale-safe bound implementation with the IR where the mathematical contracts agree.

title: Canvas and decal scope collection repeat the same algorithm
proof: Both traverse design bulkstreams, match native stream identities, filter a scope kind, parse matching scopes, and sort/deduplicate image IDs. Their kind, parser, and output record differ.
impact: Stream matching and ordering rules have two maintenance owners. No current behavior error was demonstrated.
fix: Factor the shared stream/scope traversal; keep each image parser and record type distinct. Avoid a new public trait solely for this pair.

title: Similarity admission accepts a 60-degree sheared frame
proof: Columns (1e-6,0,0), (0.5e-6,sqrt(0.75)*1e-6,0), and (0,0,1e-6) pass as a similarity. The first two columns are 60 degrees apart. The dot-product threshold has units of length rather than squared length and floors scale at 1.
impact: ensure_similarity and deflection scaling can accept a transform that changes angles and cannot be represented by one uniform scale.
fix: Test orthogonality on normalized columns and compare column lengths with a dimensionally consistent tolerance.

title: Normal transformation silently returns an unnormalized vector
proof: Uniform transform scales 1e200 and 1e-200 return normal lengths 1e200 and 1e-200 instead of 1. The manual norm overflows/underflows, then the fallback returns the transformed vector unchanged.
impact: Placed triangulation normals violate normalization expectations. Extreme finite scale is required for this witness.
fix: Normalize using the shared scale-safe vector operation; do not treat failed normalization as a successful unit vector.

title: Three TechDraw list validators duplicate structure admission
proof: The three functions repeat single-root admission, list-tag checks, count parsing, element counting, child tag/type checks, and record dispatch. The literal names and record validator differ.
impact: A structural validation fix requires three parallel edits. Record-specific validation must remain separate.
fix: Use one private typed-list traversal with explicit list/record names and a record-validation callback.

title: Edge and vertex appearance transfer repeat style and binding construction
proof: The two functions repeat payload-prefix selection, provider identity handling, packed RGBA conversion, nonnegative size filtering, appearance construction, and binding creation.
impact: Provider/style behavior can drift between edge and vertex presentation. Target type, style property, and labels are legitimate differences.
fix: Share style/binding construction around explicit appearance targets and metadata; preserve the domain-specific target selection.

title: Text B-rep table readers repeat their envelope parser
proof: All three find start/end table tokens, take the declared count, bound minimum token consumption, parse indexed rows, and reject trailing tokens. Only section labels and row parsers differ.
impact: The same framing, allocation, and trailing-data rules are maintained three times.
fix: Share the table envelope reader and pass the owned row parser; keep curve and surface grammar code separate.

title: Both quadratic solvers change roots when all coefficients are scaled
proof: x^2-1 returns [-1,1]. Multiplying every coefficient by 1e-10 yields [-0] in both solvers; multiplying by 1e-20 yields no roots. Absolute floors control degree and discriminant classification.
impact: Analytic intersection and sketch equation candidates are lost or fabricated by a representation-only scaling. Later geometric checks may reject false candidates, but cannot recover omitted roots.
fix: Normalize coefficient magnitude first, use a scale-relative discriminant bound and stable quadratic roots, and retain each caller's admission checks.

title: Circle–circle intersection fabricates a unique tangent point
proof: Two circles of radius 1e-6 with centers (0,0) and (1e-6,0) have two intersections. The function returns the single point (0.5e-6,0), which lies on neither circle.
impact: The scale.max(1) height tolerance turns a genuinely ambiguous trim intersection into a purported unique coordinate.
fix: Normalize the geometry and distinguish two crossings from a tangent with a relative error bound; forward-check any returned point against both circles.

title: Legacy curve and surface array lookup duplicate the same ownership checks
proof: The signatures and lookup/uniqueness/parent/completeness logic are identical. Only the array name, crv_array versus srf_array, differs.
impact: The exact same source ownership invariant has two implementations.
fix: Replace the pair with one array lookup parameterized by the array name; update callers directly.

title: JT transform parsing rejects finite orthogonal scales through f32 norm overflow
proof: Byte fixtures differing only in uniform diagonal scale accept 1 but reject 1e20 and 1e-30. Squaring finite f32 rows produces infinity or zero.
impact: Valid finite transform carriers become unavailable to the JT presentation path. This is an extreme-scale parser limitation.
fix: Promote the norm/rank arithmetic or scale the rows before computing lengths and orthogonality.

title: Linked and target index row projection duplicate source resolution
proof: Both traverse indexed sections, derive storage/base offsets, locate the opening block, absolutize the frame, resolve control-index references, assign row ordinals, and collect records. Scanner and output wrapper differ.
impact: Offset/provenance and reference admission changes must be mirrored across both paths.
fix: Share the section/frame projection flow with explicit row construction; retain distinct row scanners and wire types.

title: Class and field registry collection duplicate merge policy
proof: Both independently merge framed and indexed definitions into a BTreeMap keyed by entry/offset, prefer framed records, and construct the same ordinal/provenance/tail fields.
impact: Source precedence, identity, and registry-tail handling have duplicate owners.
fix: Share the registry collection and precedence operation. Keep class/field record types and labels explicit.

title: Legacy B-rep vertex averaging can create infinity from finite endpoints
proof: The current accumulator and final mean expressions turn two identical endpoints (1e308,0,0) into (infinity,0,0). Their exact mean is the same finite endpoint.
impact: Legacy topology assembly creates a nonfinite point before transfer. The source arithmetic is reproduced; a complete legacy archive fixture was not constructed.
fix: Use scale-safe averaging or scaled sums, including mixed-sign inputs; retain source tolerances and finite admission.

title: Optional localizer curve and surface readers duplicate child framing
proof: Both read an anonymous child, apply the same version gate, read a presence boolean, parse the payload, skip trailing child bytes, and advance the parent. Labels and the payload parser differ.
impact: Child-boundary and version handling have two copies. The NURBS payload parsers themselves are distinct.
fix: Use one private optional-child reader taking the owned payload parser and diagnostic label.

title: Arc tessellation reports zero sagitta for a nonzero chord error
proof: For span 1e-5, radius 1e12, and requested tolerance 1e-9, the cap is 4096 segments. Reported error is 0, while 2*r*sin(span/(4*n))^2 gives 7.4505805969e-7.
impact: Downstream error accounting underestimates the actual approximation error. The witness is a very large-radius, short-angle arc; no ordinary-radius corpus frequency is claimed.
fix: Compute sagitta through the stable sine-squared identity, use a stable inverse for segment selection, and propagate the actual error when the cap is reached.

title: Seeded surface projection wrapper adds no contract
proof: The wrapper forwards all three arguments unchanged to nurbs_surface_parameter_near_point and returns its result unchanged. Caller residual checks remain outside it.
impact: The extra name hides the true numerical owner and adds an unnecessary maintenance step.
fix: Remove the wrapper and have its callers use the owning IR function directly.

title: Ellipse and support-cone reconstruction retain manual unsafe lengths
proof: ellipse_to_nurbs accepts a unit major radius but rejects 1e200 and 1e-200 with unit normal and ratio 0.5, although all output coordinates can remain finite. The text and binary support-cone branches repeat the same squared-major-length calculation.
impact: The earlier normalized-direction repair did not fix these independent radius computations. Valid extreme-scale ellipse/cone geometry can be dropped. The ellipse is probed; cone branches are confirmed by source inspection.
fix: Use scale-safe lengths for major/minor vectors, preserving the native-to-mm conversion and existing geometry admission.

title: Mesh volume and centroid depend on translation
proof: A closed tetrahedron with vertices (0,0,0),(2,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1) has volume 1/3 and centroid (0.5,0.25,0.25). At translation (1e6,1e6,1e6), the routine switches to an area centroid with relative x=0.5833333333. At translation 1e9 it reports volume about 666666666.7.
impact: STEP validation-property comparisons can report false mismatches for the same solid moved in model space. The origin-based triple products cancel; the absolute-coordinate volume epsilon also changes centroid selection.
fix: Compute moments relative to a local reference point and restore the translation afterward; base degeneracy thresholds on local extent, with stable accumulation.
